reading.body:
H.R. 6879 is a Democratic-only bill on integrated circuit export restrictions, and the only lobbying filed on it comes from an AI security group.

The sponsor is Gregory Meeks, and all seventeen cosponsors are Democrats. The bill's own text is tagged to national security and exports, which places it in the same policy channel as chip export controls rather than in AI model regulation. The subject is the hardware layer: integrated circuits, the physical input that compute depends on.

One outside organization, the Alliance for Secure AI Action, filed two lobbying filings naming the bill. A filing that names a bill shows the bill was an issue in the lobbying, not the position taken on it, so the data does not say whether the group supports or opposes the measure. It also does not say how much was spent, or whether any chipmaker, cloud provider, or data center operator lobbied on it.

What the record covers is sponsorship, cosponsorship, and the fact of two lobbying filings. It does not cover committee action, floor votes, amendments, or the bill's outcome, and the latest status date given is 2025-12-18. The absence of Republican cosponsors is a fact about this bill, not evidence about where either party stands on export controls generally.

summary: H.R. 6879, RESTRICT Act Restoring Export and Security Trade Restrictions for Integrated Circuit Technologies Act. Latest status date 2025-12-18. Issues tagged from the bill's own text: national security and exports. 2 lobbying filing(s) for 2025 or later name it.
